The relevant facts in brief are that an FIR No.261/83 came to be registered against the petitioner stating therein that after having discharged his duty as the Conductor on 22.09.1983 on Jaipur-Gwalior route, he was supposed to deposit the bag, tickets and cash on or before 24.09.1983 but, the same was not deposited till 06.10.1983 and therefore, committed embezzlement.

After investigation, the charge-sheet was filed against him under Sections 409, 419 & 420 IPC whereunder, the charges were also framed.

trial Court, vide its judgment dated 10.11.1999, convicted and sentenced the petitioner as under:-

Learned counsel for the petitioner, eschewing merits of the case, would submit that the incident is about of 42 years old and he was dismissed from service on account of his misconduct within three months of joining.

He further submits that the petitioner is aged about 70 years, has served the sentence of one month and twenty two days and therefore, prays that while maintaining the conviction, the substantive sentence be reduced to the period already undergone enhancing the fine component reasonably and suitably.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the prayer.
Heard.
Considered.

The petitioner is facing trauma of pendency of this criminal case for last about 42 years and now, is aged about 70 years being 28 years of age at the time of his arrest. Further, indisputably, he was dismissed from service after rendering only three months' service.

Out of the maximum sentence awarded to (Uploaded on 09/10/2025 at 11:15:31 AM) [2025:RJ-JP:40909] (4 of 6)
Hukam Singh vs State (2025:Rj-Jp:40909) on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196507527/
2
[CRLR-876/2005] him of one year under Section 409 IPC, he has already served the sentence of one month and twenty two days.

Their Lordships have held in the case of, Jaydev Shrichand Danani (supra) as under:-
"2. Learned Counsel for the appellant has only prayed for reduction of sentence so that the appellant is not incarcerated at such distance of time.
The offence took place way back in July 1969.
No purpose would be served now in incarcerating the appellant at this stage.
Yet the law must have its course.
Section 409, I.P.C. leaves no choice with the Court, but to award some imprisonment besides imposition of fine.
We are not apprised as to whether the appellant has suffered any incarceration during the stage of investigation.

If he has, then the custody so suffered, which is reckonable, shall be taken to be the imprisonment already undergone for the offence committed and we reduce the period of imprisonment to that period while sustaining that of fine.
But in case the appellant has not suffered any imprisonment so far, then we reduce his sentence till the rising of the Court while sustaining that of fine.

To fulfil either purpose, we direct the Special Judge, District Banaskantha, Palanpur to summon the appellant and to verify these facts and should it be necessary, to keep him imprisoned till the rising of the Court as ordered as the second alternative.
With these directions this appeal is disposed of."

Thus, in the aforesaid case, looking to the fact that the offence was committed almost 23 years ago,
the sentence was reduced to the period already undergone and if no sentence was served, till rising of the Court.

In the case of Ramji Lal (supra), in view of the fact that the incident was about 13 years old and the petitioner was dismissed from Government service, the substantive sentence of one and a (Uploaded on 09/10/2025 at 11:15:31 AM) [2025:RJ-JP:40909] (5 of 6) [CRLR-876/2005] half years granted under Section 409 IPC was reduced to the period already undergone, i.e., ten days.
As already observed in the instant case, the incident is about of 42 years old and the petitioner has already served the substantive sentence of one month and twenty two days out of the maximum sentence of one year and therefore, in the backdrop of the aforesaid precedential law, this Court deems it just and proper to accept and allow the prayer made by his counsel.

Accordingly, this criminal revision petition is partly allowed in following terms:-
1. While maintaining the conviction recorded by the learned trial Court vide its judgment dated 10.11.1999 and upheld by the learned appellate Court vide its judgment dated 29.08.2005, the substantive sentence is reduced to the period already undergone.
2. The fine part is enhanced to 10,000/- in all.
